explanation: The earliest known rules for calculating with zero as a number in its own right come from the Indian mathematician Brahmagupta, in a book of AD 628.

claims.text: Zero separates the positive numbers from the negative numbers on a number line.
One and one half are positive numbers and minus one is negative, so none of them divides the two sets.
The earliest known rules for arithmetic with zero as a number appear in Brahmagupta's Brahmasphutasiddhanta, written in AD 628.
